locator.section: 8.2 Product stability -- Charge competition in OE(+.) decompositions: Stevenson's Rule

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.3 row 1, arrow labeled 'i' (inductive). n-butyl methyl ether molecular ion; the C-O bond cleaves and the two incipient fragments compete for the charge. THIS branch: charge migrates to the butyl fragment giving C4H9+ (25%) with loss of the neutral methoxy radical .OCH3. Printed IE(C4H9.)=8.0 eV < IE(.OCH3)=8.6 eV, so per Stevenson's rule the lower-IE butyl fragment wins the charge. Book draws 0 arcs (summary equation, no curved arrows on the page); the single heterolytic C-O cleavage arrow (both sigma electrons of bond 4-5 onto O5) is reconstructed for electron balance. LOCALIZATION: the page prints (+.) over the C-O region (mobile-charge notation) -- a carbon there would be over-valent, so the ionization is localized at the ether oxygen (lowest-IE n orbital), giving the arrows a valid origin.

Cross-linked MOD rule IMS_8_3_ind (equation 8.3, cleaves the C-O bond). MISMATCH: the rule localizes (+.) on the alpha carbon and emits BOTH fragments as cations -- C4H9(+) AND CH3-O(+) -- so its RHS carries charge +2 and radical count 2 from a +1 / 1-radical reactant; it is charge- and spin-non-conserving and is dropped by the conservation guardrail. It fuses the two competing charge outcomes (this 25% C4H9+ branch and the 1% OCH3+ branch of 8.3b) into one non-physical step. Does NOT match this substrate. See rule_mismatches.

Book prints '25%' relative abundance under C4H9+. observed_mz 57.0699 is the curator-computed electron-mass-corrected monoisotopic m/z of C4H9+; the page prints only the % abundance and the fragment IE (8.0 eV), no m/z.
